newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open 0.68 percent higher on Wall St.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open 0.68 percent higher on Wall St.

text.p: French shares opened 0.68 percent higher on Tuesday on the back of a 1.72 percent overnight gain on Wall Street.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 18.38 points at 2,711.47 at the opening while the CAC-40 futures contract was up seven points at 2,691.

Bond futures and PIBOR interest rate futures were slightly weaker. Two overnight opinion polls gave the centre-right government coalition a lead in the run-up to the parliamentary election of May 25 and June 1.
French April inflation, 0.9/1.0 percent up year-on-year, was in line with expectations and bond traders said the figures showed there was no price pressure as demand remained subdued.
Main events due this week are the April U.S. producer price index on Wednesday, seen unchanged, and the consumer price index, seen up 2.6 percent year-on-year, due on Thursday.
The Federal Reserve's policy making FOMC meets on May 20 to deliberate interest rates.
The CAC-40 index, while having regained the important 2,700 level on Monday, still has some way to go to the all-time high of 2,736.71 of March 11.
Polls by Louis Harris and BVA gave the centre-right coalition a lead over the Socialist opposition.
These polls follow a weekend Sofres study which gave the majority a comfortable lead after a series of polls which indicated that the race was tightly contested.
Jacques Langlade-Demoyen, of CSFB in London, said the polls reflected recent disunity in the opposition with the Communist Party unwilling to play second fiddle to the Socialist party.
Jacques Chahine Finance said that if the conservatives won the elections, the CAC could go to over the 3,000 level while if the Socialists won it would fall to 2,400.
Shares in Alcatel Alsthom SA gained over four percent on Tuesday morning on the back of a 12.1 percent rise in its first quarter sales.
At 0829 GMT, the share was up 4.34 percent at 673 francs. While sales were up, new orders were slightly down. All sectors contributed to the sales rise apart from the batteries sector.
